import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The problem asks whether the word problem is decidable for every group with one defining relation
in the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most $n$, for $n \geq 3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

/--
Is the word problem decidable for every group admitting one defining relation in the variety of
soluble groups of derived length at most $n$, where $n \geq 3$?

For finite rank $m$ and relator $r \in F_m$, this group is
$F_m/(F_m^{(n)}\langle\!\langle r\rangle\!\rangle)$. Since both factors in the denominator
are normal, their product is represented by their join. A word is encoded as a list of generators
with a Boolean recording the sign of each letter.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n m : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ r : FreeGroup (Fin m),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        FreeGroup.mk w ∈ derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r} := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.16»
modeling_decisions: Represented finite-rank free-group input words concretely as `List (Fin m × Bool)` and interpreted them via `FreeGroup.mk`, because `ComputablePred` requires a `Primcodable` input and Mathlib has no such instance for `FreeGroup` itself.

Represented the kernel of the relatively free one-relator soluble group as `derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}`. This is the subgroup product from the decomposition because both constituent subgroups are normal.
Used the unary identity language as the word problem: a concrete word is accepted exactly when its image in the quotient is the identity.

Read “the variety of soluble groups of derived length n” as derived length at most n, as specified by the fixed decomposition, and universally quantified all `n ≥ 3`, finite ranks `m`, and relators `r`.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

The variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$ consists of the
groups $G$ with $G^{(n)} = 1$, where $G^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th term of the derived series.
A group with $m$ generators and a single defining relation $r$ in this variety is the
quotient $F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$ of the free group $F_m$ of
rank $m$ by the product of its $n$-th derived subgroup and the normal closure of $r$.
Its word problem asks for an algorithm which decides, for a word $w$ in the generators
and their inverses, whether $w$ represents the identity of the group.

For $n = 1$ (abelian groups) and $n = 2$ (metabelian groups) the word problem for such
groups is known to be soluble; the problem asks about $n \geq 3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

/--
Is the word problem soluble for every group admitting a single defining relation in
the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$?

That is, for every $n \geq 3$, every rank $m$ and every element $r$ of the free group
$F_m$ on $m$ generators, is there an algorithm deciding, for a word $w$ in the generators
of $F_m$ and their inverses, whether $w$ lies in the normal subgroup
$F_m^{(n)} \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$, i.e. whether $w$ represents the identity of
the group $F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$?

Words are modelled as lists in `Fin m × Bool`, the letter `(i, true)` standing for the
`i`-th generator and `(i, false)` for its inverse, and the word `w` represents the element
`FreeGroup.mk w` of the free group.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        FreeGroup.mk w ∈ derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r} := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.16»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The decomposition table's single slot and its notes match the statement; the file conforms to them.
modeling_decisions: 'Variety of soluble groups of derived length n' is read as the variety 𝔄^n of groups G with G^{(n)} = 1 (derived length ≤ n), as in the decomposition notes; a group with one defining relation r in it is F_m / (F_m^{(n)} · ⟨⟨r⟩⟩), modelled as the quotient of FreeGroup (Fin m) by the (normal) join derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}.

The group is taken to be of finite rank m (m : ℕ arbitrary, including m = 0, where the word problem is trivially decidable and does not distort the universal claim); the word problem is only meaningful for finitely generated groups.

The word problem is formalized as ComputablePred on words List (Fin m × Bool) (letter (i, true) = generator i, (i, false) = its inverse; verified FreeGroup.of i = mk [(i,true)] and (of i)⁻¹ = mk [(i,false)]), with w ↦ FreeGroup.mk w ∈ N. This is used because FreeGroup has no Primcodable instance; it is also the classical formulation of the word problem (decide whether a word represents the identity). Membership in N is equivalent to the image being 1 in the quotient group since N is normal.

The terse notebook entry is read as the single yes/no question 'is the word problem soluble for every such group, for every n ≥ 3', with all quantifiers (n ≥ 3, m, r) after answer(sorry); answer(False) then means some n ≥ 3, m, r yields an unsolvable word problem.

AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic / computability) and 20 (group theory). The module docstring mentions that the cases n = 1, 2 are known to be soluble (abelian; finitely generated metabelian groups are residually finite and finitely presented in 𝔄^2).

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the
variety of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

Let $\mathfrak{A}^n$ be the variety of soluble groups of derived length at most
$n$. A group with a single defining relation in $\mathfrak{A}^n$ is a group of
the form
$$G = F_m \big/ \bigl(F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle\bigr),$$
where $F_m$ is the free group of finite rank $m$, $F_m^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th
term of its derived series (so that $F_m / F_m^{(n)}$ is the free group of
$\mathfrak{A}^n$ of rank $m$), and $r \in F_m$ is the defining relator. The
word problem for $G$ asks for an algorithm deciding, for a word $w$ in the
generators $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$, whether $w$ represents the
identity of $G$, i.e. whether $w \in F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$.

The problem asks whether this word problem is soluble for every such group when
$n \geq 3$. For $n = 1$ the groups are abelian and the word problem is trivially
soluble; for $n = 2$ the groups are finitely generated metabelian groups, which
are residually finite (P. Hall) and recursively presented, so their word problem
is soluble.

*References:*
- [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46), Problem 3.16.
- [P. Hall, *On the finiteness of certain soluble groups*, Proc. London Math.
  Soc. (3) 9 (1959), 595–622](https://doi.org/10.1112/plms/s3-9.4.595), for the
  residual finiteness of finitely generated metabelian groups.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

/--
The normal subgroup $F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ of the free
group $F_m$ on `Fin m`, generated by the $n$-th derived subgroup $F_m^{(n)}$ and
the normal closure of the relator $r$. The quotient of $F_m$ by this subgroup is
the group with the single defining relation $r = 1$ in the variety
$\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length at most $n$.

Since both $F_m^{(n)}$ and $\langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ are normal, their
product coincides with their join in the lattice of subgroups.
-/
def oneRelatorSolubleRelations (n m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)) :
    Subgroup (FreeGroup (Fin m)) :=
  derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}

/-- The subgroup of relations is normal, so the quotient by it is a group. -/
@[category API, AMS 20]
instance oneRelatorSolubleRelations_normal (n m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)) :
    (oneRelatorSolubleRelations n m r).Normal :=
  haveI := derivedSeries_normal (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n
  Subgroup.sup_normal _ _

/-- The relator is a relation. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem mem_oneRelatorSolubleRelations_self (n m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)) :
    r ∈ oneRelatorSolubleRelations n m r :=
  Subgroup.mem_sup_right (Subgroup.subset_normalClosure rfl)

/-- The group with one defining relation in the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ lies in
$\mathfrak{A}^n$: its $n$-th derived subgroup is trivial. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem derivedSeries_quotient_oneRelatorSolubleRelations (n m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)) :
    derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m) ⧸ oneRelatorSolubleRelations n m r) n = ⊥ := by
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective _) n, eq_bot_iff,
    ← QuotientGroup.map_mk'_self (oneRelatorSolubleRelations n m r)]
  exact Subgroup.map_mono le_sup_left

/--
Is the word problem soluble for every group admitting a single defining relation
in the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$, where
$n \geq 3$?

Here the group is $G = F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$
for a finite rank $m$, a derived length $n \geq 3$ and a relator $r \in F_m$. Its
word problem is soluble if the set of words $w$ in the letters
$x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$ (encoded as lists in `Fin m × Bool`) that
represent the identity of $G$, i.e. satisfy
$w \in F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$, is a computable predicate.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        FreeGroup.mk w ∈ oneRelatorSolubleRelations n m r := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.16»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The single-slot decomposition and its notes (variety A^n = derived length ≤ n, finite rank m, universal quantification over n ≥ 3, m, r, ComputablePred on words) match my reading of the statement.
modeling_decisions: 'Word problem for a group' is read as the terse Kourovka form of the yes/no question 'Is the word problem soluble for every group with one defining relation in the variety A^n, n ≥ 3?'; hence answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ n ≥ 3, ∀ m, ∀ r, … . If the answer were to depend on n (e.g. yes for n = 3, no for n = 5), this single Prop records only the 'for all n ≥ 3' answer.

Decidability is non-uniform: ComputablePred is asserted for each fixed group (fixed n, m, r), which is the classical meaning of 'the word problem for a group G'. A uniform version (computable in (m, r, w)) would be stronger and is not what the statement asks.

'Soluble groups of derived length n' is taken as the variety A^n (derived length ≤ n), so the relatively free group is F_m / F_m^{(n)} with F_m^{(n)} = derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n; the one-relator group in the variety is F_m / (F_m^{(n)} ⟨⟨r⟩⟩). The product of the two normal subgroups is written as the lattice join ⊔ (equal for normal subgroups); an API instance and a test lemma check normality and that the quotient has trivial n-th derived subgroup.

Words are represented as List (Fin m × Bool) (letters x_i^{±1}) mapped by FreeGroup.mk, so that the word problem is literally a predicate on words and Mathlib's existing Primcodable instances suffice; no Primcodable instance on FreeGroup is needed.

The rank m is finite (free group on Fin m) and ranges over all m, including m = 0; the relator r ranges over all of F_m including r = 1 (both degenerate cases have decidable word problem, so they do not affect the answer).
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic/computability) and 20 (group theory) were chosen, following the repo's BranchingVAS.lean use of tag 3 for decidability questions.

It is a thin wrapper around derivedSeries ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r}.

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety of
soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

The variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length (at most) $n$ consists of
the groups $G$ with $G^{(n)} = 1$, where $G^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th derived subgroup. A group
with $m$ generators and a single defining relation $r$ in this variety is
$$G = F_m / \bigl(F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle\bigr),$$
where $F_m$ is the free group on $x_1, \dots, x_m$ and $r \in F_m$; equivalently, $G$ is the
quotient of the free soluble group $F_m / F_m^{(n)}$ of derived length $n$ by the normal
closure of the image of $r$. The word problem for $G$ asks for an algorithm that decides,
for a word $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$, whether $w$ represents the identity of $G$,
that is, whether $w \in F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$.

For $n = 1$ and $n = 2$ the word problem for such groups is known to be decidable; the
problem asks about $n \geq 3$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

/--
Is the word problem decidable for every group admitting a single defining relation in the
variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$, for every $n \geq 3$?

Here $m$ is the (finite) number of generators, $r \in F_m$ is the single defining relation,
and the group in question is $G = F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$.
A word in the generators $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$ is modelled as a
`List (Fin m × Bool)`, which `FreeGroup.mk` sends to the element of $F_m$ it represents.
The word problem for $G$ is decidable when the predicate "the word $w$ represents the
identity of $G$", i.e. $w \in F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$, is a
computable predicate on words.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (n : ℕ), 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        FreeGroup.mk w ∈ derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ Subgroup.normalClosure {r} := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«3.16»

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 3.16

by M. I. Kargapolov

The word problem for a group admitting a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, $n \geq 3$.

Let $\mathfrak{A}^n$ be the variety of soluble groups of derived length (at most) $n$ and
let $F_m$ be the free group of finite rank $m$. A group with a single defining relation
$r \in F_m$ in the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ is the group
$$G = F_m / \bigl(F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle\bigr),$$
where $F_m^{(n)}$ is the $n$-th term of the derived series of $F_m$; equivalently, $G$ is
the quotient of the free soluble group $F_m / F_m^{(n)}$ of derived length $n$ by the normal
closure of the image of $r$. The word problem for $G$ asks for an algorithm deciding, for a
word $w$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}$, whether $w = 1$ in $G$.

The problem asks whether the word problem is decidable for every such group when $n \geq 3$.
For $n = 1$ and $n = 2$ the word problem is known to be decidable.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«3.16»

open Subgroup

variable (m n : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m))

/-- The normal subgroup $F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle$ of the free group
$F_m$ of rank `m` generated by the $n$-th derived subgroup $F_m^{(n)}$ together with the
relator `r`. -/
def relators : Subgroup (FreeGroup (Fin m)) :=
  derivedSeries (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n ⊔ normalClosure {r}

instance : (relators m n r).Normal :=
  haveI := derivedSeries_normal (FreeGroup (Fin m)) n
  sup_normal _ _

/-- The group with generators $x_1, \dots, x_m$ and the single defining relation $r = 1$ in the
variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$ of soluble groups of derived length $n$, that is,
$F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$. -/
abbrev OneRelatorSolubleGroup : Type :=
  FreeGroup (Fin m) ⧸ relators m n r

/--
Is the word problem decidable for every group with a single defining relation in the variety
of soluble groups of derived length $n$, for every $n \geq 3$?

For the group $G = F_m / (F_m^{(n)} \cdot \langle\langle r \rangle\rangle)$, the word problem
is the predicate on words $w$ over the alphabet $\{x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_m^{\pm 1}\}$
(elements of `List (Fin m × Bool)`, read in $F_m$ via `FreeGroup.mk`) that holds exactly when
$w$ represents the identity of $G$. Decidability of the word problem for a fixed group $G$
means that this predicate is computable.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«3.16» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ n, 3 ≤ n → ∀ (m : ℕ) (r : FreeGroup (Fin m)),
      ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin m × Bool) =>
        (FreeGroup.mk w : OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) = 1 := by
  sorry

/-- The relator `r` is trivial in `OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r`. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem coe_relator_eq_one : (r : OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) = 1 :=
  (QuotientGroup.eq_one_iff r).2 <| mem_sup_right <| subset_normalClosure rfl

/-- `OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r` is soluble of derived length at most `n`, i.e. it lies in
the variety $\mathfrak{A}^n$. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem derivedSeries_eq_bot : derivedSeries (OneRelatorSolubleGroup m n r) n = ⊥ := by
  rw [← map_derivedSeries_eq (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective (relators m n r)) n,
    Subgroup.map_eq_bot_iff, QuotientGroup.ker_mk']
  exact le_sup_left

end Kourovka.«3.16»

The terse entry is read as the yes/no question "is the word problem decidable for all such groups?", with universal quantifiers over n ≥ 3, m and r placed after `answer(sorry)`. Consequently `answer(True)` = decidable for every n ≥ 3, every m, every r; `answer(False)` = some such group has undecidable word problem. A reading that asks separately for each n (e.g. as a set of n) was not used.

The word problem is the non-uniform one (for each fixed group G = G(m,n,r), the predicate on words is computable), which is the standard meaning of 'the word problem for a group'; the uniform version (algorithm taking r as input) is not what is stated.
